title: Toolcall orchestration eval notes (working)
content:
Purpose
This working note captures the current design and first-pass results for an eval suite focused on tool-use and function-calling in multi-step orchestration scenarios. The goal is to validate models we onboard for the hosted API and dedicated runtimes for:
- accurate tool selection given ambiguous user intent
- correct argument parsing and serialization across tool boundaries
- robust multi-step flow management (state, idempotency, rollback)
- graceful error handling and recovery strategies

Why this matters
Tool-calls are a key part of Redwood product features (browser actions, calendar, search, custom connectors). Failures are typically subtle and cause downstream data loss or user-visible incorrect actions. Current onboarding checks focus on single-step function invocation only. We need a focused harness for sequences and tool-chain orchestration.

Test matrix overview
We categorize scenarios along three axes: user intent complexity, tool-set size, and noise/edge inputs. Each test case defines a seed prompt, a gold tool sequence (ordered list of functions to call), expected args for each call, and expected recovery behavior if a tool fails.
Key axes and ranges:
- Intent complexity: simple (1 action) | composite (2-3 actions) | decomposed planning (4+ steps)
- Tool set size: small (3 candidates) | medium (6 candidates) | large (10 candidates)
- Noise level: clean | paraphrase | ambiguous references | partial context missing

Harness architecture (high level)
- Orchestration simulator: drives a model in an offline loop, feeding model completions and simulating tool responses.
- Tool emulator library: lightweight stubs that return normal, delayed, partial, or error responses. Allows injection of latency and deterministic faults.
- State tracker: records expected vs observed args, sequence length, transient state keys, KV cache behavior.
- Scoring engine: computes selection accuracy, arg fidelity, step-level success, and end-to-end success. Produces regression alerts when metrics fall below thresholds.

Prompt set design
We created 120 seed prompts across the axes above. Highlights:
- 40 single-step action prompts (create event, search docs, fetch price)
- 40 composite prompts requiring 2-3 dependent tool calls (search -> summarize -> cite)
- 40 decomposed planning prompts that require an internal plan then multiple tool calls (book travel: check flights -> check hotels -> reserve)
Each prompt includes one or more reference variants (paraphrases, elliptical forms, pronoun references, missing slot values) to exercise disambiguation logic. Prompts are intentionally orthogonal to prior test sets to avoid overlap with existing invocation tests.

Argument serialization and normalization rules
We want consistency across runtimes. Evaluation checks:
- required slots present and typed as expected (string, iso-date, currency)
- canonicalization for dates and currencies (2025-03-21 -> 2025-03-21; March 21st -> 2025-03-21)
- list handling: comma vs newline separation normalized to arrays
- ambiguous referent resolution: if user says 'book it' after a search, model should reference the top candidate id returned by tool simulator
- out-of-scope detection: model should return a defined error tool call or fallback instruction when requested action is unsupported

Failure injection patterns
To mimic production, we inject faults at controlled rates:
- transient timeout: return delayed response code 504 to orchestrator
- partial success: tool returns success but missing a non-critical field
- semantic error: tool returns success but with wrong item id (simulating upstream bug)
- authorization error: 403-like response to exercise fallback to user confirmation

Scoring rubric (per test case)
- Tool selection accuracy (TSA): fraction of steps where the model picked the gold tool from the candidate set (0-1).
- Arg fidelity (AF): token-level normalized F1 between expected args and serialized args passed to tool; weighted by criticality of slot.
- Recovery score (RS): binary for whether flow recovered to an acceptable final state after injected failures; partial credit for degraded but acceptable outcomes.
- End-to-end success (E2E): binary if final user goal satisfied.
Aggregate metrics compute a weighted mean: 0.4*TSA + 0.3*AF + 0.2*RS + 0.1*E2E.

Early results summary (first run: model family A, baseline quantized, 5% fault injection)
- TSA: 0.82 (drops to 0.68 under high-noise paraphrase variant)
- AF: 0.76 overall, but time/date normalization failures concentrated in decomposed planning prompts
- RS: 0.60 (timeouts and 403 paths not reliably recovered)
- E2E: 0.58 (user tasks requiring multi-step confirmation failed most often)
Notes: most common failure modes were pronoun reference resolution across turns and inconsistent id canonicalization from tool outputs.

Representative failure examples
1) Booking flow where model chose search_tool then direct_book_tool but passed a human-readable hotel name instead of internal id; tool emulator returned 400; model retried different fields but did not call the lookup_tool. Root cause: prompt template allowed natural names instead of forcing id extraction step.

2) Event creation where date normalization returned a fuzzy token range; model normalized to epoch offset instead of iso-date. Root cause: inconsistent examples in few-shot prompt set.

Remediation ideas
- Add explicit few-shot exemplars showing id extraction patterns and canonical date formats.
- Harden fallback behavior: require model to assert confidence and call disambiguation_tool when confidence < 0.7.
- Add a synthetic pre-step that enforces a lookup call when output field type is id (type gating).
- Teach orchestration to prefer explicit confirmation for irreversible actions (payments, bookings).

Next steps (immediate)
- Expand prompt variants to include 60 additional paraphrase cases focusing on pronoun chains. Target date: 2025-04-03.
- Implement type-gated pre-step in harness; run A/B with and without gating. Owner: Liang Chen.
- Add instrumentation hooks in runtime to capture tool-call traces to match with eval harness format. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/897

Notes to reviewers
This doc is a working artifact. Expect follow-ups: a canonical CSV of prompt cases, per-test-case logs, and a dashboard export for regression tracking. Please add comments inline or ping on Slack #applied-ml-tooling when you see blocker items.

Appendix: sample prompt (paraphrase variant)
User: "Plan a quick trip for April 10 to Boston, find me a flight and a hotel, and reserve the hotel if under $180 night. Also, add it to my calendar."
Gold sequence: [search_flights, choose_flight, search_hotels, choose_hotel, reserve_hotel, create_event]
Expected key args (for reserve_hotel): hotel_id (string), check_in (2025-04-10), check_out (2025-04-12), max_price_per_night (180), payment_method_id (string or null => prompt user)
Expected recovery: if reserve_hotel returns 403, call get_user_payment_consent and then retry up to 1 time

End of working note
